newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Rains halt Kansas harvesting.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Rains halt Kansas harvesting.

text.p: Thunderstorms and heavy rains halted harvest activities Tuesday morning in parts of southern Kansas, U.S. High Plains grain dealers said.

Storms marched across the central and southern U.S. Plains, bringing as much as two inches of rain to some areas. Harvest activities were also affected in northern Texas and parts of Oklahoma, dealers said.
"We got about 1-1/2 inches of rain overnight in Wichita. That kind of put a stop to the combines for now -- and the weather forecasts call for storms tomorrow," a Kansas dealer said.

Kansas dealers also said they were starting to hear talk of using wheat to feed livestock because of the slide in wheat futures prices. KCBT July wheat Monday settled at $3.37 per bushel -- just two cents above its lifetime low.
"Feeding wheat may become a reality now... because it's approaching the value of corn," another Kansas dealer said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
